title: this Pointer and Member Access
learningObjectives: Explain this pointer and member access.
Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: this is a pointer to the current object inside a non-static member function. It can disambiguate members from parameters and return the current object reference.
understand.whyItMatters: It clarifies instance access and fluent APIs.
understand.explain: Use this only when needed; static member functions have no this pointer.

examples.title: Use this to disambiguate
examples.explanation: this->value identifies the member rather than parameter.

examples.title: Return current object reference
examples.code: class Builder{public:Builder& setA(int n){a=n;return *this;}int a=0;};\nBuilder b;b.setA(4);

examples.title: Instance identity
examples.code: class Box{public:bool same(const Box& other)const{return this==&other;} };\nBox a;std::cout<<a.same(a);
examples.explanation: this is compared with another object's address.

examples.title: No this in static
examples.code: class Math{public:static int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}};\nint v=Math::add(2,3);
examples.explanation: Static member function has no current instance.

examples.title: Member parameter shadow
examples.code: class User{public:User(int id):id(id){}int getId()const{return this->id;}private:int id;};
examples.explanation: this-> explicitly refers to the object's member.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five this Pointer and Member Access examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating this pointer and member access in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.explanation: this refers to the current instance.
Static functions have no current object.
Current object reference can be returned.
this is a pointer to the current object.
